messages:
amy_support: FYI customer on prod reported a sudden p99 jump after we onboarded lotus-v2 yesterday. They see 3–5x p99 on long-context (>50k tokens) requests, and a few API 502s. Posting logs and a repro.

mike_ingest: ugh, did lotus-v2 include the new tokenization glue we shipped last week?

anika_runtime: yes lotus-v2 switched to token_glue_v3. We thought it improved encoding speed but maybe the long-prefix path regressed.

amy_support: customer repro steps (they gave these):
1) Set model=lotus-v2, context=60k tokens, streaming=true
2) Send a 3MB prompt with lots of whitespace/newlines
3) Observe p95 ~800ms -> p95 ~2.8s, p99 ~7–9s and occasional 502s in API responses

amy_support: sample request_id: req_2026_00012345, logs: 
```
ERR: tokenizer: split_fragment_count spike: 124K fragments
WARN: kvcache: miss_rate increased from 0.04 -> 0.61 for req_2026_00012345
ERR: runtime: stream handler closed early: net/http: timeout
```

anika_runtime: requesting traces. @ci_bot can you pull trace for req_2026_00012345 and the internal span breakdown?

ci_bot: trace pulled: https://ci.internal/traces/req_2026_00012345 (access: eng). Exported span durations: tokenize 2800ms, encode->kvpopulate 3400ms, route->serve 120ms.

mike_ingest: tokenize 2.8s is the obvious hotspot. Token_glue_v3 must be creating a fragmentation explosion on whitespace-heavy inputs; we saw similar in perf test but not at scale because test inputs differed.

amy_support: customer also reported billing anomalies — several of the slow requests were retried by their client and duplicated tokens got counted. They provided invoice rows — looks like 12x token charge for some retries.

raj_support_mgr: prioritize as SEV2 — impact: single large customer affected, risk of wider p99 regression. Steps: triage, short-term mitigation, fix rollout plan.

anika_runtime: short-term mitigations I can do without code change:
- pin lotus-v2->lotus-v2-tokenizer-v2 (fallback tokenizer) for the affected shard via routing rule
- temporarily enforce strict max_input_tokens=40k for lotus-v2 on hosted tier (reject >40k)
- enable optimistic KV prefetching TTL bump to reduce cache miss storm

mike_ingest: to add: create a traffic-split Canary that sends 10% traffic to 2.2.1 (tokenizer-v2) variant and 90% to v3, monitor p95/p99. If good, flip.

anika_runtime: I can push a routing override now. Need approval for rejecting >40k — may break some customers. Amy, do they tolerate temporary truncation?

amy_support: customer says they can temporarily chunk on client side if we ask, they'd prefer not to be billed for retries though. We can credit them.

raj_support_mgr: approve routing override + quota truncation for affected account + refund. Go ahead with canary. Keep me posted every 30m.

deploybot: routing-override applied: lotus-v2 shard s3 -> split 90/10 v3/v2 at 174500./apply/8821 :white_check_mark:

anika_runtime: monitoring dashboards: p95 down from 2.8s -> 1.1s in last 6m for that shard, p99 trending down but still elevated (1.8s). KV miss rate also falling. Can we throttle client-side retry window too?

amy_support: I asked customer to pause retries while we stabilize; they agreed. Also opened a billing ticket to credit duplicate token charges.

mike_ingest: next steps for root cause: reproduce locally with whitespace-heavy long prompt using token_glue_v3, instrument fragmentation algorithm, add unit/perf test for 50–100k whitespace sequences. If confirmed, either fix glue algorithm or add fast-path for long whitespace runs.

anika_runtime: quick repro help: run: 
```
python tools/repro_longctx.py --model lotus-v2 --tokenizer token_glue_v3 --length 60000 --gap_policy whitespace-heavy
```
I ran it, fragmentation count exploded; we can prune empty fragments before encoding which cuts tokenize time ~3x in my quick patch. I'll open PR for hotfix (non-breaking change) and a follow-up more thorough rewrite.

ci_bot: perf-run queued: perf/lotusv2/glue-v3-prune-empty/174500/1

amy_support: customer confirmed latency improvement after canary, still verifying p99 tail. They asked for ETA on permanent fix and a note on billing credits.

raj_support_mgr: proposed comms: update customer in 2 hours with mitigation summary + billing refund + ETA for permanent fix (48–72h target). Amy, pls draft.

amy_support: drafted: "We've applied a routing override to use the prior tokenizer variant for a portion of traffic, implemented a temporary max_input_tokens limit, and will refund duplicated token charges. Eng team has a hotfix PR under test; we aim to roll a permanent fix within 48–72 hours." Ping if edits.

mike_ingest: QA note: when we roll the hotfix, ensure migration plan for existing KV entries; pruning fragments may change hash mapping, so we'll need backward-compatible normalization or a one-time cache flush for affected models. Coordinate with infra for controlled cache warmup to avoid a second spike.

anika_runtime: noted. I'll include a staged rollout: canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with cache-prewarm steps and automated rollback on p99 increase.

deploybot: hotfix PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/lotus-tokenizer/pulls/87 (tests pending)

ci_bot: perf-run completed: prune-empty reduces tokenize time from 2800ms -> 850ms on repro. kv miss side-effect minimal in perf-run.

amy_support: sharing update with customer now. They asked also for prevention: can we add synthetic long-whitespace tests to our onboarding harness so new tokenizers don't regress downstream?

mike_ingest: absolutely — add a long-whitespace scenario to model-onboard perf-suite and require no >1.5x increase vs prior tokenizer on that scenario for gated onboarding.

raj_support_mgr: good. Amy, set expectation + credit. Anika, mike, aim to have hotfix canary in next 12h and full rollout in 48h. Keep thread updated.

amy_support: will do. Final note: billing ticket created #BILL-3421, customer credited provisional amount. Closing loop later after final numbers. :white_check_mark:
